sources.title: Royal Museums Greenwich, Traders: the East India Company and Asia
sources.note: Institutional gallery text checked through full indexed original; direct fetch failed. Charter paragraph and object labels for Jamsetjee Bomanjee Wadia and Edward Barlow. Do not use its shorthand assertion of corporate abolition in 1858: parliamentary legal history distinguishes dissolution in 1874.

sources.title: UK Parliament, Parliament and the East India Company
sources.note: Direct institutional text read, opening and Financial crisis, Parliament steps in, More government control. Its reductive gunpowder explanation for Plassey is not used.

sources.title: UK Parliament, Joint Committee on Consolidation Bills, evidence of 28 April 2008
sources.note: Direct transcript read, Q3 to Q5: Law Commission witness Roger Teasdale distinguishes the 1858 government transfer from full dissolution in 1874. Used for those institutional transitions, not conversational guesses about prime ministers.

sources.title: Victoria and Albert Museum, Tipu’s Tiger
sources.note: Direct object interpretation read. Opening mechanism description and Tipu Sultan section explain the 1799 assault, killing, looting and removal to London. Mysore craftsmanship is explicitly attributed to the conquered court, not the Company.

sources.title: Royal Museums Greenwich, Cutty Sark history: Opium wars and the tea trade
sources.note: Direct institutional section read. Indian-grown opium sold onward by merchants to Chinese smugglers; Chinese suppression in 1839 and British war. Cutty Sark itself is later than Company rule and is not attributed to this period.

sources.title: Richard Mulholland, Changing Displays at the Nehru Gallery: Conservation of Company Paintings at the V&A (2013)
sources.note: Full indexed original article read; canonical direct URL returned 403. Defines Indian artists/European patrons, imported and local supports, burnishing, and identifies A Doctor with a Female Patient, Lucknow circa 1850. The latter was in an independent Indian kingdom before the 1856 annexation, not assumed Company territory at creation.

sources.title: Victoria and Albert Museum, Kalighat painting
sources.note: Direct article read, opening dates 1830s to 1930s and Origins of Kalighat painting. Early market/production context used; illustrated late nineteenth-century subjects are not backdated to Company rule.

sources.title: Census of India 1961, Madras City Report, Part X-(I), volume IX
sources.note: Official retrospective report checked through indexed original, Conservancy section: 1776 George Town rules on carts, cows and household cesspools. Direct PDF retrieval timed out. The introductory account of 1961 sanitary work is not used as evidence of Company-era practice. Exact query: site:censusindia.gov.in/nada "Governor of the East India Company" "scavengers".

sources.title: Museums Victoria, NU 46270: Company rupee with frozen date 1835
sources.note: Direct object catalogue read, Reverse Description and Significance. Exact English lettering, catalogue transliteration Yek Rupiya and translation One Rupee; F mint mark dates actual striking 1836 to 1840. The apparent 1845 typo in the quoted heading for the 1835 Act is not used.

sources.title: Presidency University, Brief History of Presidency
sources.note: Direct institutional history read: 1817 foundation, initially Hindu male pupils, 1855 government institution open to young men of all communities, subjects. No claim of universal access or first-ever Asian education.

sources.title: Bethune College, institutional introduction and Principal’s Desk
sources.note: Indexed original institutional text read; direct opening returned challenge. Distinguishes Calcutta Female School established in 1849 from college founded in 1879. No pupil totals or unsourced first-school superlatives used.

sources.title: Jayanta Bhattacharya, The Hospital Transcends into Hospital Medicine, Indian Journal of History of Science 52.1 (2017), 28 to 53
sources.note: Direct scholarly PDF read, printed pages 46 to 49. Named courses from 1836 to 1838; clinical teaching, 1839 dispensary figures, early anesthesia and marginalization of Indian medical traditions. Avoids disputed precise day and first-ever claims for dissection.

sources.title: Shamita Chatterjee, Ramdip Ray and Dilip Kumar Chakraborty, Medical College Bengal: A Pioneer Over the Eras (2013)
sources.note: Authors are affiliated with the college. Indexed original text checked; direct current retrieval returned browser check. The hospital building was inaugurated in 1852 for 350 patients. Only this architectural/care claim used; not its sweeping story of ancient medical stagnation.

sources.title: John Shoolbred, Report on the progress of vaccine inoculation in Bengal, November 1802 to end of 1803 (published 1805), Wellcome Collection
sources.note: Direct primary-text transcription read, printed page 27, canvas 43. Author addresses parental anxiety, children’s suffering, blindness and scars, while promoting vaccination. Period claims of perfect safety and fixed death ratios are not repeated.

sources.title: British Library and University of Exeter, Famine Tales: Sources at the British Library
sources.note: Direct institutional archival guide read. IOR/E/4/621 and /622 contain charges/countercharges over grain monopoly and oppression during 1770 famine; IOR/H/799 records Kyd’s 1786 garden proposal for food plants. Claims remain at catalogue-description level, not a purported reading of the underlying manuscripts.

sources.title: National Army Museum, Why did the Indian Rebellion happen?
sources.note: Direct museum text read, Discontent, Rulers join the rising and opening. Annexations, pay, promotion and religious fears; different Indian units and rulers made different choices. Avoids the museum’s simplistic no-male-heir gloss of the doctrine of lapse.

proposedOverrides.name: British East India Company
proposedOverrides.summary: A trading corporation that became a colonial territorial power; Company government ended in 1858.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: New exact-ID card, no aliases. Distinct from British Raj; historical life and imported interval explicitly separated.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Only a coarse 1815 snapshot is present, carried through 1878; no geometry repair or successor edge requested. Lucknow circa 1850 painting is explicitly from pre-annexation Awadh. English coin lettering and catalogued Persian transliteration are attested; no reconstructed original glyphs.
